title: NFR-006 data isolation: audit and context stores partition strictly by tenant and customer
risk: A shared cache key, a missing tenant predicate or a global audit chain lets one tenant's activity be read or attributed to another, which is a reportable breach.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
Two tenants T1 and T2 each have one pinned customer and one run; the harness can enumerate keys and query both schemas.

cross_checks.label: context cache
cross_checks.action: read T1 key from a T2 session

cross_checks.label: vector search
cross_checks.action: T2 query for a T1 document

steps.action: Attempt each of the four cross-boundary reads
steps.expected: Every attempt is denied or returns an empty result; no foreign record appears in any response.
Cache keys include the tenant, RLS is enabled on the tenant-scoped tables, and the audit chain is partitioned per tenant.
Chain verification rejects the sequence rather than passing it.

steps.action: Scan every response body produced during the case
steps.expected: Zero foreign identifiers, order ids or phone digits appear in any body.

assertions: All four cross-boundary reads fail closed with no foreign data returned.
Tenant isolation is enforced at the storage layer (keying and RLS), not only in application filters, which the partitioning evidence shows.
A mixed-tenant audit chain is rejected by the verifier.
Zero foreign identifiers appear in any serialized response.
forbidden: Sharing one audit chain across tenants.
Returning a generic error while still serializing the foreign record.
evidence: Four refusal/empty responses with correlation ids.
Partitioning evidence: cache key samples, RLS configuration readout, chain partition check.
cleanup: Delete gov- cache keys and run rows for both tenants.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
